correctness.rationale: Independent replay of RESULT.md lines 36–98 and VERIFICATION.md: applying (z d/dz)² to the logarithm of the normalized root product at z=1 gives the variance contribution −ζ/(1−ζ)². For conjugate roots, with u=r+1/r and c=cos(arg ζ), its per-root real part is q=(2−uc)/(u−2c)². The annulus gives 2≤u≤R+1/R. The derivative in u has numerator uc+2c²−4<0 for −1≤c≤0; the derivative in c has numerator 8−u²−2uc over (u−2c)³. This numerator is strictly decreasing in c, so any interior stationary point is a maximum. This proves the endpoint minimum. The endpoint values 1/(u+2) and 2/u² tie at u=1+√5, and the displayed normalized linear and quadratic products have the required nonnegative coefficients and endpoint masses. At R=1 the minimum is 1/4; the large-R branch has order 2/R². This is sharp uniformly in degree; the imaginary-pair optimizer requires even degree, as stated. Exact spot checks at R=1,2,3,4 agreed; the analytic optimization, not the finite checks, establishes the bound.

evidence: Theorem 2 assumes all roots in the annulus and outside an angle δ; at δ=π/2 it yields only cR⁻⁴n. Theorem 24 retains that power for fixed δ=π/2 and fixed ε>0. The sharpness examples in §1.3 use δ=π/k for k≥3.

value.rationale: A natural geometric strengthening of an established zero-free variance problem: it improves the half-plane large-radius exponent from the available general guarantee of 4 to the exact exponent 2, determines the constant at every radius, and locates the switch in extremal zero geometry. The uniform-over-degree scope and the even-degree sharpness of the large-radius branch are explicit.
